doc.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002

title: First paid gigs: Pat Patterson, the Drum Club and Rose Murphy
summary: His first money came from after-hours piano-drum jobs and subbing for Saunders King's drummer; Rose Murphy stole tips.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Well let me ask you, the first time you made money playing the drums. Do you recall that?

Oh yeah. Let’s see. I guess it was with Patterson. Pat Patterson played the piano. And he was a good piano player, schooled in theory and harmony. And Pat used to get gigs at these after hour places so we worked at a place called Minnie’s Can Do, up on Fillmore Street in the Western Addition, after hours, just piano and drums. And I think I made two bucks. And then there was a club called the Drum Club. And it was — the building is still there but it’s under another name, that was right around the corner from the union, it was on Turk and Jones. And when Saunders King’s band would get a job his drummer would take off and I’d sub for him. So that job I’d get I think one or two dollars. And the piano player was Rose Murphy. And I’d see her playing, and there would be a quarter, somebody put a quarter down there, and if I turned my head and looked back the quarter was gone. She’d steal the tips. She was an old timer you know.
You didn’t get anything by her I would guess.
No. She would. She’d steal the tips.
You were still a teenager, right?

Yeah, and I had a little part time job. And I just wanted to play you know. I didn’t — but for her I guess many times you had many performers and band leaders that they were, when it came to the money they were really tight fisted and a lot of times they would exploit their people. You’ve heard that story many times. © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
